title: GitHub Has an Availability Problem. Is It Time to Look Elsewhere?
excerpt: GitHub has been having enough outages lately that people are starting to ask whether it makes sense to look elsewhere. Ever since Github got acquired by ...
content_html:
Dhruv

Home Blog Now

17 Aug, 2026

GitHub has been having enough outages lately that people are starting to ask whether it makes sense to look elsewhere.

Ever since Github got acquired by Microsoft it started getting bloated and enshittified - it lost its direction and doesn't seem to care about its customers. And Github is probably not the only one - there are many other examples.

We got to have a kill switch for this - when do we as a community say enough is enough and switch from GitHub. If a tool constantly proves unreliable, keep using it is not logical.

I really hope Github pulls up its socks and really addresses the problems - the network effect will not last for long if you keep having outages.

As pointed out pertinently on hn - "But there isn’t one obvious transition candidate, so the diaspora is finding itself spread across a bunch of disparate places and services. The stated need they satisfy (source control with a web interface and some technical features, like pull requests with reviews) will be fulfilled. But those emergent features like a core community and default expectation of where you can find someone will fade. And that is a very real loss for all of us."

content_html_zh:
Dhruv

现在主页博客

17 Aug, 2026

GitHub 最近发生了足够多的中断，人们开始问是否有必要去其他地方寻找。

自从 Github 被微软收购后，它就开始变得臃肿和虚伪——它失去了方向，而且似乎并不关心它的客户。 Github 可能不是唯一的 - 还有很多其他例子。

我们必须为此设置一个终止开关 - 作为一个社区，我们什么时候会说“够了”并从 GitHub 切换过来。 如果一个工具不断被证明不可靠，那么继续使用它是不合逻辑的。

我真的希望 Github 能够振作起来，真正解决问题——如果持续出现中断，网络效应不会持续太久。

正如 hn 中指出的那样——“但是没有一个明显的过渡候选者，所以侨民发现自己分散在一堆不同的地方和服务中。 他们所满足的既定需求（具有 Web 界面的源代码控制和一些技术功能，例如带有评论的拉取请求）将得到满足。 但那些新兴的功能，比如核心社区和对在哪里可以找到某人的默认期望将会消失。 这对我们所有人来说都是一个非常现实的损失。”
